thread:
sam: quick follow-up from today's all-hands about burn and procurement. a couple things my team needs clarified: new approval thresholds, p-card changes, and how to get something expedited if it's blocking a customer demo. cc @camille @rahul

camille (CFO): headline: runway ~15 months at current burn, and we've tightened approval bands to reduce non-essential spend. short answers first, details below.

sam: can you list the approval bands clearly?

camille (CFO): yes. effective immediately: under $3k = manager approval (no procurement ticket); $3k to $25k = procurement + finance approval required; $25k to $250k = procurement + finance director sign-off; over $250k = CFO + legal + procurement and vendor must finish enterprise onboarding. these replace the old thresholds.

sam: what's changed for p-cards?

camille (CFO): p-card single-transaction cap = $3k default. monthly rolling cap = $12k. exceptions via Spend Request form require two approvers. p-cards cannot be used to onboard new vendors for fees > $3k; use PO/contract route.

rahul (procurement): process notes: vendor onboarding SLA = 7 business days for standard vendors, 15 business days for elevated-risk. provide the full onboarding packet in the portal; incomplete packets will pause approval.

marie: for urgent infra (GPU/cloud) bursts needed for demos, whats the expedite path?

camille (CFO): submit an "expedite" Spend Request, tag "expedite-infra", and ping @rahul + @lina. procurement can provision a temporary PO or approve a p-card exception up to $10k while onboarding proceeds. CFO approval still required for > $25k but we aim to unblock infra within 48 hours for justified emergencies.

lina (ops): ops also maintains a small contingency fund for sub-$15k urgent purchases. DM ops@redwood with a 1-2 sentence justification and ETA for procurement completion to access it.

tom (finance-bot): automated guardrail alerts will DM users at 80% of monthly p-card cap and notify approvers.

olivia (legal): contracts note: any agreement with indemnity, customer data residency, or SLA obligations must route to legal even if under $25k. attach the contract intake template.

sam: can you paste the Spend Request link and an email subject template for procurement pings?

camille (CFO): link: https://internal.redwood.com/spend-request (internal). Email template:

```
Subject: Spend Request - ProjectName - VendorName - Est $XXXX - Expedite: yes/no
Body: short summary, justification, cost center, requested approvers, attach onboarding packet if vendor
```

camille (CFO): i'll update the procurement runbook and drop a short doc in #docs after this.

rahul (procurement): operational tip: if replacing a vendor, mark "replacement" in the form and attach termination plan for the outgoing vendor to speed review.

marie: question re: Dedicated/reserved capacity (often > $250k). any special handling?

camille (CFO): reserved capacity is enterprise-level: sales ops prepares term sheet, procurement + legal negotiate, CFO signs financial terms. multiyear commits or > $250k need CFO approval and run-rate impact analysis (how it affects monthly burn and runway).

sam: hiring controls tied to this?

camille (CFO): hiring is scoped down for non-critical roles. critical hires require VP + people ops + finance sign-off. priority for product/infra hires that improve unit economics or unblock revenue.

rahul (procurement): i'll host office hours tomorrow 11:00-11:30 for anyone with pending requests  drop in or add to the calendar.

lina (ops): reminder: to use the ops contingency fund DM me with justification and the expected procurement completion ETA.

tom (finance-bot): note: this thread will be archived into the spend-controls doc set automatically.

sam: thanks everyone :thumbsup:
